explanation: Fires only at D2 (zero at D1/GO). Its magnitude comes from one gate: this trial is a1 -> S1 (common, seen at D2) and the previous trial was also a1 -> S1 rewarded. The base term alone gives dev R^2 beyond timing 0.21. Inside that context, the size falls off steeply with episode trial (it interacts with timing; the additive phase x decile baseline does not capture this): it is small on trials 0-4, peaks around trials 5-20, and decays toward zero by about 60. That episode-trial interaction, plus a term for the window first trial (previous trial unknown), takes R^2 to about 0.47. The ideal-observer S1 belief log-odds adds a small positive graded effect (+0.005). Two-back rewards, belief_cover, start_high and the hidden good state / since_rev add essentially nothing (<0.003). Test R^2 beyond timing is 0.537 (dev 0.537), above the profile additive all ceiling of 0.34 and the all-observed ceiling of 0.26. Unexplained: some windows with long a1 S1 rewarded streaks stay at zero while others sit near 0.38. Observed variables do not predict which; the earlier value/policy-based explanation probably covered this, and that is the main loss from going observed-only.

issues: The reported numbers reproduce. The six claimed terms give test R^2 beyond timing 0.537. The base context term alone (D2 x a1->S1 x last trial a1 S1 r) gives 0.211.

The episode-time shape checks out when the context term is split into ep_trial bins on test: weights are 0.150 (trials 0-4), 0.217 (5-9), 0.216 (10-19), 0.193 (20-29), 0.136 (30-44), 0.042 (45-59) and 0.013 (60+). It is low early, peaks at 5-20 and is near zero by 60. The decline is closer to concave than linear: a squared term adds about +0.003.
The belief effect is real but tiny: removing the belief term drops test R^2 from 0.537 to 0.533. 'Grows with S1 belief' in the label overstates something worth +0.004.

The misses output shows a systematic offset error. D1 and GO are under-predicted by +0.005 on average (the true value there is exactly 0), and every non-context D2 cell is over-predicted by about -0.014. This is an intercept/baseline artifact, not a wrong cue. Adding one '(phase != D2)' term removes it (mean errors fall to about 0.000) and raises test R^2 from 0.537 to 0.587. The reported score therefore understates what this explanation can reach.

The worst misses are whole windows of rewarded a1->S1 streaks where the actual value is 0 but the prediction is 0.17-0.30, mostly at episode trials 4-20. None of these predicts them (each adds under 0.002): start_high, good state, p_s1, since_rev, belief_cover, belief < 0.5, a two-back pattern, streak length or valid/d1_err. The original explanation already admits this gap, and it is an episode-level bimodality rather than a phase or previous-trial class.
No future variables are used; the claim checks out.
